title: The Wolf of the Weeping Wood
premise: Hazel Quintana, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead in his carvings, has spent years guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains while hiding the gift that ruined his family. When a mute child arrives at his door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Hazel learns the boy is the last living seal of an ancient covenant between the human realm and the Weeping Wood, where the wolf-spirits were betrayed and bound centuries ago. Hunted by the Crown's Inquisitor Veyra—who wants to consume the covenant's power for herself—Hazel and the boy flee into the mountains, gathering three scattered covenant-bones and confronting the truth that Hazel's own ancestor led the original betrayal. At the Wood's heart, Hazel must choose between destroying the wolf-spirits as duty demands or reforging the covenant at the cost of his own life; he offers himself, but the wolves, moved by the boy's forgiveness, accept only his hearing instead, leaving Hazel deaf to the dead yet bound as the new Warden of the Wood.
about_author: Edmund Iversen is a former cartographer of mountain passes who turned to fantasy after a decade mapping terrain no official chart would admit existed. He writes in a cabin above the treeline, where he claims the wind still speaks a language predating kingdoms.

chapters.title: The Bone That Sang
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. In his workshop, Hazel carves a dead woman's finger-bone and hears her final secret, which he sells quietly to her grieving daughter. The beat establishes his gift as both livelihood and curse, ending when a knock comes at his door on the coldest night of the year.

chapters.title: A Child Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. A mute boy stands on his doorstep, barefoot in snow, unharmed by cold. When Hazel touches the boy's carved wooden wolf-token, he hears not one voice but thousands layered together—a language that predates every kingdom he knows. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Consulting the bones of his grandmother, Hazel learns the boy is a living seal of the Covenant of Thornfell, broken when human ancestors betrayed the wolf-spirits of the Weeping Wood. His own family name appears in the betrayal. Beat: shame and denial.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Summons
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Inquisitor Veyra arrives in town, elegant and terrifying, asking after 'a stolen relic.' Hazel lies to her face and feels her see through it. He packs that night, taking the boy. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Hazel leads the boy up the forbidden passes only smugglers know, using tricks learned from the dead. The boy begins speaking single words of Hazel's tongue. First ambush by Veyra's riders; they escape by collapsing a bridge. Beat: reluctant trust forming.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Greyfell
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. They shelter with Maren, an exiled priestess who recognizes the boy and reveals the first covenant-bone lies in a drowned chapel below Greyfell lake. She warns Hazel: the covenant demands a price from whoever reforges it. Beat: hope shadowed by foreboding.

chapters.title: Beneath the Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. A freezing dive among sunken bones yields the first covenant-bone—and the drowned dead scream warnings about 'the wolf who weeps.' Veyra's men reach the shore above. Beat: triumph undercut by terror.

chapters.title: Veyra's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Veyra. The Inquisitor interrogates captured smugglers and reveals her motive: she was once a village girl the Wood's wolves spared, and she believes consuming the covenant will end all fear forever. Beat: villain made sympathetic, ambition revealed as corruption.

chapters.title: Voices in the Snow
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Lost in a whiteout, Hazel follows the boy's instinct to safety and realizes the boy is leading him, not the reverse. Around the fire, the boy speaks his first full sentence: 'They are waiting.' Beat: tenderness, role reversal.

chapters.title: The Weeping Wood's Edge
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. They reach the forest border where trees bleed sap like tears and the dead grow silent—the Wood eats ghosts. A wolf-spirit scout watches them, neither attacking nor fleeing. Beat: awe and the sense of being judged.

chapters.title: The Wolf Who Weeps
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The ancient wolf-mother Ulva appears, scarred by old iron, and shows Hazel the betrayal in memory: his ancestor Quintana drove the sealing stake. She gives him until the full moon to bring the remaining two bones—or the boy dies as the seal breaks. Beat: guilt made flesh.

chapters.title: Prisoner of Two Courts
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Held gently captive in the Wood, Hazel bonds with the boy and learns the wolves' side: their imprisonment bleeds them slowly, and their rage grows less controllable each year. Beat: empathy for the 'monsters,' loyalty beginning to shift.

chapters.title: Escape and Betrayal
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Veyra assaults the Wood with fire and iron; in the chaos Hazel flees with the boy—but abandons a wounded young wolf to do it. Beat: self-loathing; the cost of survival measured in a look of betrayal.

chapters.title: The Second Bone
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Following his grandmother's riddling bones, Hazel retrieves the second covenant-bone from a barrow guarded by his ancestor's restless ghost, who begs forgiveness rather than fights. Beat: ancestral reckoning; Hazel accepts his inheritance of guilt.

chapters.title: Maren's Sacrifice
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Veyra captures Maren and trades her life for the bones. Hazel refuses; Maren frees herself by burning the Inquisitor's armory and dies in the blaze, passing Hazel a map to the third bone. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Deciphering Maren's map, Hazel learns the truth: the covenant can only be reforged by a willing sacrifice—one who carries the betrayer's blood must give what they most treasure. Beat: quiet acceptance; Hazel stops running.

chapters.title: Full Moon Rising
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Racing the moonrise through the Thornfell passes with Veyra's surviving hunters behind him, Hazel reaches the Wood's heart carrying the boy and two bones. The third bone, he now understands, is the boy himself. Beat: breathless momentum toward climax.

chapters.title: The Heart of the Wood
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. At the shattered covenant-stone, Veyra arrives and seizes the bones, beginning to consume their power; the Wood convulses, wolves and humans alike screaming. Hazel shatters her concentration by giving her back her oldest memory—the night the wolves spared her. Beat: climax ignites.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Broken open by her own past, Veyra falters between vengeance and mercy. Hazel places the boy—willing, unafraid—on the stone and offers his own blood and his hearing in the boy's stead. Ulva must choose: justice or renewal. Beat: the thematic crux, love outweighing duty.

chapters.title: The New Covenant
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The covenant reforges: the boy becomes free and merely mortal, the wolves regain their true forms, and Hazel's gift passes from him into the Wood itself—he will never hear the dead again. Veyra, emptied, walks into exile rather than face judgment. Beat: catharsis and cost.

chapters.title: Silence and Saplings
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Spring comes to the Weeping Wood; trees weep clear water now instead of tears. Hazel, deaf to ghosts for the first time in his life, grieves the silence even as he treasures it. The boy chooses to stay with him. Beat: bittersweet peace.

chapters.title: Warden of the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Months later, Hazel serves as Warden between realms, guiding travelers honestly instead of smuggling them, while the boy—now called Rowan—learns bone-carving without the burden of voices. On the wind, Hazel almost hears something kind. Final beat: a life remade, loyalty and truth finally aligned.
